(i) Yes, the conjecture is true for any multiple of 9. When digits are reversed, sum of digits remain the same.
(ii) Yes, any shuffle of the digits is still a multiple of 9, because any rearrangement of the digits does not change the sum of the digits.
5. If 48a23b is a multiple of 18, list all possible pairs of values for a and b.
Ans. 48a23b is a multiple of 18 if it is multiple of both 2 and 9.

```txt
For any number multiple of 2, ones place must be an even number
So b = 0, 2, 4, 6, 8
For any number to be multiple of 9, sum of digits must be a multiple
of 9.
So, 4 + 8 + a + 2 + 3 + b = 17 + a + b must be multiple of 9.
For b = 0
a + b + 17 = a + 17 is a multiple of 9
a + 17 ≠ 9 as a will be negative.
a + 17 = 18,
So, a = 1
For b = 2
a + b + 17 = a + 19 is a multiple of 9.
a + 19 ≠ 9, 18; as a will be negative.
So, a + 19 = 27, a = 8
If a + 19 = 36, then a = 17. But a is a digit so a ≠ 17
The possible pairs are (1, 0) (8, 2) (6, 4) (4, 6) and (2, 8)
```
6. If 3p7q8 is divisible by 44, list all possible pairs of values for p and q.

**Ans.** 3p7q8 is divisible by 44, means divisible by 11 and 4. For divisiblility by 4, last two digits must be divisible by 4 So possible q8 are 08, 28, 48, 68, 88. For divisibility by 11, difference between sum of the odd place digits and even place digits must be 0 or multiple of 11 Sum of odd place digits = 8 + 7 + 3 = 18 Sum of even place digits = p + q Difference is 18 − (p + q) Let k = 18 − (p + q) = 0 or a multiple of 11.
